name: Rhodolite-Scorch
description: Rhodolite-Scorch burns in shades of rose and raspberry, its desert surface stained by rhodolite garnet dust that covers everything in a fine pink-red powder. Dust seas stretch to every horizon, interrupted only by deep canyon systems whose walls reveal layers of compressed garnet sand in shades ranging from pale pink to deep magenta. An ancient meteor crater in the southern hemisphere serves as the only significant landmark, its rim the highest point on the planet.

The thin atmosphere provides minimal thermal regulation, creating scorching days that give way to bitterly cold nights. The garnet dust is beautiful but abrasive, working its way into every seal and joint of equipment exposed to the surface winds. At dawn and dusk, the dust-laden sky turns the color of blood rubies, and the entire landscape seems to pulse with warm light.

Hardy flora survives in the canyon depths where moisture condenses on the cool rock walls, tough succulent species with deep root systems and thick, waxy leaves. These plants are increasingly rare, pressured by the planet's slow desiccation as it loses atmospheric moisture to space. A pirate operation has established itself in the crater, using its natural walls and the planet's remoteness as protection from law enforcement patrols.

Rhodolite-Scorch's solar potential is exceptional, and several energy companies have expressed interest in orbital solar collection arrays. The pirate presence complicates any legitimate development, and the criminals have shown willingness to defend their territory with force. The endangered flora may hold medicinal value, but accessing the canyons means passing through territory claimed by people who shoot first. The rose-colored dust settles on everything equally, pirate ships and research probes alike.
